描述_ZN: The Galloping Horses" scroll, modern, painted by Xu Beihong, on paper with color, 89.2 cm in length and 81.8 cm in width.　　Self-titled: "In the fourth month of the twenty-eighth year, Beihong visited Xingzhou. Inscription: "Wang Sun of the East China Sea" in white and rectangular. There is also an inscription by Han Huaijun, with three seals in vermilion: "Huaijun is the most precious", "Han Jun Gong, the thirteenth grandson of Siyu Fun Zhai", and "Idiot Porcelain Drunken Pottery". 　　Twenty-eight years that refers to the twenty-eighth year of the Republic of China (1939), Xu Beihong was 44 years old.　　Xu Beihong in Singapore (Singapore), and the local scribe Han Huaijun formed a deep friendship, and for Han Huaijun created a number of excellent works, this is one of the works he gave to Han.　　The picture depicts a stallion galloping on autumn grass. Xu Beihong's painting of horses is based on respect for traditional Chinese and Western painting techniques, outside the teacher, focusing on life, forming their own distinctive characteristics: the head of the horse is often left a blank, or a white powder, to show the highlights of the horse's head to enhance the sense of three-dimensionality and the hard texture of the horse's head. The horse's neck and belly are drawn with a soft brush and a thick ink stroke, with thick, elastic curves to show the strength of the muscles. The mane and tail of the horse are mixed but not chaotic in the application of ink, and their strokes of reality and emptiness, dry and wet ink, express the flowing and unrestrained mane of the horse as it gallops.
